title: Conjecture 1.1 (Las Vergnas–Meyniel Conjecture A)
statement_text: For every $t$, all the $t$-colourings of a graph with no $K_{t}$-minor form a single equivalence class.
context_text: Las Vergnas and Meyniel introduced this in 1981 as a reconfiguration counterpoint to Hadwiger's conjecture, after proving the analogous result for $K_5$-minor-free graphs. It neither implies Hadwiger's conjecture nor is implied by it.
paper_contribution: Disproves this conjecture by constructing, for every $\varepsilon>0$ and all large enough $t$, a graph with no $K_t$-minor whose $(\frac{3}{2}-\varepsilon)t$-colourings are not all Kempe equivalent (Theorem 1.3).
paper_title: On a recolouring version of Hadwiger's conjecture

title: Conjecture 1.2 (Las Vergnas–Meyniel Conjecture A')
statement_text: For every $t$ and every graph with no $K_{t}$-minor, every equivalence class of $t$-colourings contains some $(t-1)$-colouring.
context_text: Proposed by Las Vergnas and Meyniel in 1981 as a related but weaker statement than Conjecture 1.1, assuming Hadwiger's conjecture holds.
paper_contribution: Disproves this conjecture as a consequence of Theorem 1.3, which produces a frozen colouring with no path to a $(t-1)$-colouring in its Kempe equivalence class.
paper_title: On a recolouring version of Hadwiger's conjecture

title: Conjecture 1.4 (Las Vergnas–Meyniel Conjecture C)
statement_text: For any $t$, any graph that admits a quasi-$K_{t}$-minor admits a $K_{t}$-minor.
context_text: Las Vergnas and Meyniel introduced the notion of quasi-$K_p$-minor (where the bags $B_i$ need not be connected but each $B_i\cup B_j$ must induce a connected subgraph) and conjectured it is equivalent to the standard minor. The conjecture had been verified for $t\leqslant 10$.
paper_contribution: Strongly disproves this conjecture for large $t$ via Theorem 1.5, which constructs graphs admitting a quasi-$K_t$-minor but no $K_{ct}$-minor for some explicit $c<1$; the precise infimum $c$ is left as Question 1.6.
paper_title: On a recolouring version of Hadwiger's conjecture

title: Question 1.6
statement_text: What is the infimum $c$ such that for any large enough $t$, there is a graph that admits a quasi-$K_{t}$-minor but no $K_{ct}$-minor?
context_text: A graph admits a $K_p$-minor if it has $p$ non-empty, pairwise disjoint bags $B_1,\dots,B_p$ of vertices, each inducing a connected subgraph, with an edge between $B_i$ and $B_j$ for all $i\ne j$; it admits a quasi-$K_p$-minor (a notion of Las Vergnas and Meyniel) if it has $p$ non-empty pairwise disjoint bags such that $B_i\cup B_j$ induces a connected subgraph for all $i\ne j$ (the bags themselves need not be connected). A colouring is frozen if any two colour classes induce a connected subgraph; the colour classes of a frozen $p$-colouring form a quasi-$K_p$-minor. Las Vergnas and Meyniel conjectured that every graph with a quasi-$K_t$-minor has a $K_t$-minor; this is known for $t\le10$. Trivially every graph with a quasi-$K_{2t}$-minor has a $K_t$-minor (merge bags in pairs), so $c\ge\frac12$. The authors strongly disprove the conjecture: for every $\varepsilon>0$ and $t$ large enough, there is a graph with a quasi-$K_t$-minor but no $K_{(2/3+\varepsilon)t}$-minor, so $c\le\frac23$. In an addendum, they note that the same construction had been discovered independently earlier (by Reed, and by Böhme, Kostochka and Thomason), without the implications on quasi-minors.
paper_title: On a recolouring version of Hadwiger's conjecture

title: Question 1.7
statement_text: Is there a constant $c^{\prime}$ such that for every $t$, all the $c^{\prime}\cdot t$-colourings of a graph with no $K_{t}$-minor form a single equivalence class?
context_text: All colourings are proper vertex colourings. Given a $k$-colouring, a Kempe chain is a maximal connected subgraph induced by two colours (a vertex with no neighbour of the second colour is a chain by itself), and a Kempe change swaps the two colours on one Kempe chain; two $k$-colourings are Kempe equivalent if one can be obtained from the other by a sequence of Kempe changes, and 'equivalence class' refers to this equivalence on the set of $k$-colourings. Meyniel proved that all $5$-colourings of a planar graph are Kempe equivalent, and Las Vergnas and Meyniel extended this to $K_5$-minor-free graphs and conjectured that for every $t$ all $t$-colourings of a graph with no $K_t$-minor are Kempe equivalent. The authors disprove this: for every $\varepsilon>0$ and $t$ large enough there is a graph with no $K_t$-minor whose $(\frac32-\varepsilon)t$-colourings are not all Kempe equivalent (it has a frozen colouring, in which any two colour classes induce a connected subgraph), so $c'\ge\frac32$ if such a constant exists. The best known upper bound comes from the result of Kostochka and of Thomason that graphs with no $K_t$-minor have degeneracy $O(t\sqrt{\log t})$, combined with the fact that all $k$-colourings of a $d$-degenerate graph are Kempe equivalent for $k>d$.
paper_title: On a recolouring version of Hadwiger's conjecture
